big: India's real GDP grew 7.7% in FY26, up from 7.1% a year before. The economy is about ₹346 lakh crore, close to a $4 trillion size. Growth and size are two different numbers. This lesson keeps them apart.

lines: Is 7.7% the size of the economy?
No. 7.7% is speed: how fast real output grew. The ₹346 lakh crore is size: nominal GDP. Real strips out price rises. Nominal does not.

note: Figures as per the lesson text. Check current releases. Rupee moves decide the race with Japan.

q: India is 3rd by PPP and 4th–5th by nominal GDP. Why do they differ?
opts: One of them is a mistake
PPP counts only the rich few
why: PPP corrects for what money buys locally.
Both are valid measures of different things.
PPP does not count only a group of people.
Nominal GDP is measured in currency, rupee included.

q: A client says, 'Growth of 7.7% means we are the biggest economy.' What is the reply?
opts: Yes, as GDP is all that counts
Growth is speed, size is separate
why: Fast growth does not equal the largest size.
GDP has both a size and a growth reading.
Speed and size are different numbers.

pts: Real GDP removes price rises. Nominal GDP shows size.
FY26 real growth: 7.7%. Size: about ₹346 lakh crore.
Rank depends on the measure: nominal or PPP.
